features.title: Render the product entry page
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can open the app and see an X-META Video entry page instead of a blank screen or generic starter content.
verification: Open the app.
Verify the page shows the X-META Video name.
Verify the page describes AI comic drama, MV, and short-form video creation.
Verify the page does not show unrelated conversation or generic template content.
evidence: Corrected the prior basic shadcn-only treatment by adding `apps/web/src/app/animated-entry-page.tsx`, an animated X-META Video entry page adapted from the UI TripleD Hero Block shadcn/Framer Motion source pattern.

Kept `apps/web/src/app/page.tsx` as the app-root route and delegated rendering to the local animated entry page while preserving product-specific AI comic drama, MV, and short-form video creation copy.
Added `framer-motion` because the selected UI TripleD Hero Block pattern uses Framer Motion for reveal, hover, spring, and scroll indicator animation effects.
Kept UI TripleD as copied/adapted local source guidance rather than adding an opaque UI TripleD runtime dependency; local shadcn/ui components remain the component base.
Updated render tests to assert `data-uitripled-source="hero-block"` and `data-animation-runtime="framer-motion"` in addition to the required product copy and generic-content rejection.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web test` passed with 2 test files and 5 tests.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web build` passed and statically generated `/` and `/icon.svg`.

Playwright fallback with system Chrome opened `http://localhost:3000` at 1440x900 and 390x844; title was `X-META Video`, required product copy was present, UI TripleD/Framer Motion data markers were present, no generic starter/chat content was present, no console errors or page errors were reported, and there was no horizontal overflow.
Interaction check: `Review production modes` navigated to `#production-modes`; `See canvas direction` navigated to `#canvas-preview`.
Animation check: the scroll indicator changed position during a timed browser probe, confirming live Framer Motion animation was active.
`.\init.ps1` passed after implementation; Vitest ran 2 files with 5 passing tests.
features.notes: Frontend-only page shell; no backend, auth, or persistence required.

features.title: Add the create-project entry point
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can click a primary Create Project action and see clear project-start choices for comic drama, MV, or short-form video.
verification: Open the main page.
Click Create Project.
Verify project-start choices become visible.
Verify the choices are specific to comic drama, MV, and short-form video.
features.notes: This is a UI entry state only; actual project creation belongs to Feature 2.

features.title: Add recent-work entry points
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can find the recent work area and understand where existing projects can be reopened.
verification: Open the main page.
Locate the recent work area.
Verify it shows either project cards or a clear empty state.
Verify the visible action points toward opening or creating project work, not messaging.
features.notes: Use static or local placeholder data only until project persistence exists.

features.title: Add the workspace entry path
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can click an Enter Workspace action from the main page and reach a clear creative workspace entry placeholder.
verification: Open the main page.
Click Enter Workspace.
Verify the app shows a workspace entry placeholder or route target.
Verify the copy makes it clear the full workspace shell is a later feature.
features.notes: Do not implement the full canvas or app shell here; that belongs to Feature 2 and Feature 3.

features.title: Show the creation workflow preview
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can scan the main page and understand the planned flow from brief to script, storyboard, assets, audio, video, and export.
verification: Open the main page.
Verify the workflow preview includes script, storyboard, character or scene assets, audio, video, and export.
Verify the workflow reads as a production pipeline, not a messaging UI.
Verify each workflow item has concise user-facing copy.
features.notes: This is a visual orientation element only; node execution is out of scope.

features.title: Make the main page responsive
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can use the main page on desktop and mobile sizes without clipped text, overlapping controls, or hidden primary actions.
verification: Open the app at a desktop viewport.
Verify all main page sections align without overlap.
Open the app at a mobile viewport.
Verify primary actions, recent work, and workflow preview remain readable and reachable.
features.notes: Responsive behavior is part of the main page design definition of done.

features.title: Verify main page accessibility basics
features.user_visible_behavior: A keyboard user can tab through the main page actions in a sensible order and understand each action label.
verification: Open the main page.
Use Tab to move through interactive elements.
Verify focus order follows the visual layout.
Verify each button or link has a clear accessible label.
features.notes: Keep this limited to the main page; full app accessibility coverage belongs to later feature work.
